title: CI / CD
objectives: Understand CI / CD via a real-life analogy
Distinguish CI (continuous integration) from CD (delivery vs deployment)
Design a Flutter pipeline: analyze / test / build / distribute

sections.markdown:
**Think of CI / CD as the automated factory line for your code.**

Every commit enters a factory:

- **CI (Continuous Integration)** — assembly line stations: `install deps → format check → analyze → unit test → widget test → integration test → build`. A red light on any station stops the line. Goal: catch defects before they ship.
- **CD (Continuous Delivery)** — automation to PRODUCE deployable artifacts (APK / AAB / IPA) that are always ready to ship, gated by human approval.
- **CD (Continuous Deployment)** — automation to actually SHIP those artifacts to users (Firebase App Distribution, Play Internal, Prod) WITHOUT human approval.

**The rule of CI/CD:** the ONLY way code reaches users is through the pipeline. No manual builds; no laptop-uploaded APKs. **Reproducibility** = same commit produces the same artifact regardless of who ran the pipeline.

**Why every serious Flutter team has CI/CD:** without it, releases depend on 'one dev's laptop' + human memory + spreadsheet checklists. With it, every PR gets tested + every merge produces an artifact + every release is auditable. Bugs get caught in minutes, not weeks; hotfixes ship in hours, not days.

**CI (Continuous Integration)** = automatically build + test every commit + PR; block merges that break the build. **Continuous Delivery** = every green commit produces a deployable artifact; humans approve the actual deploy. **Continuous Deployment** = every green commit is automatically deployed to production. **Pipeline** = a config file (YAML) describing stages, jobs, and gates. **Tools:** GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, CircleCI, Codemagic, Bitrise, Jenkins.
## Pipeline anatomy
## Sample GitHub Actions pipeline (Flutter)

sections.code:
# .github/workflows/ci.yml
name: Flutter CI
on:
  push: {branches: [main, release/**]}
  pull_request:

jobs:
  ci:
    runs-on: macos-14   # macOS for iOS + Android via emulator
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@v2
        with: {flutter-version: '3.24.0', channel: 'stable'}

      - name: pub deps
        run: flutter pub get

      - name: format check
        run: dart format --set-exit-if-changed .

      - name: analyze
        run: flutter analyze

      - name: unit + widget tests
        run: flutter test --coverage

      - uses: codecov/codecov-action@v4
        with: {file: coverage/lcov.info}

      - name: build android bundle
        run: flutter build appbundle --release --obfuscate --split-debug-info=./symbols

      - name: build ios (release, unsigned)
        run: flutter build ipa --release --no-codesign --obfuscate --split-debug-info=./symbols

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with: {name: bundles, path: build/app/outputs/bundle/release/*.aab}

  distribute-android-nightly:
    if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
    needs: ci
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with: {name: bundles}
      - uses: wzieba/Firebase-Distribution-Github-Action@v1
        with:
          appId: ${{ secrets.FIREBASE_APP_ID_ANDROID }}
          serviceCredentialsFileContent: ${{ secrets.FIREBASE_SA_JSON }}
          groups: qa,internal
          releaseNotes: ${{ github.event.head_commit.message }}
          file: app-release.aab
      - name: upload symbols
        run: |
          firebase crashlytics:symbols:upload \
            --app ${{ secrets.FIREBASE_APP_ID_ANDROID }} ./symbols

sections.markdown: ## Secret management

sections.code:
# Never commit secrets. Use CI provider's secret store.
# GitHub: Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions
# In workflow: ${{ secrets.MY_KEY }}

# Signing keys — Android:
#   base64-encode the .jks; store as ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64.
#   In pipeline: echo $ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64 | base64 -d > /tmp/keystore.jks
#   Then Gradle uses it via signing config referencing env vars.

# Signing certificates — iOS:
#   Fastlane's `match` stores certs + provisioning profiles in an encrypted git repo.
#   Or Apple's new App Store Connect API + Xcode Cloud handles signing.

# Service account (Firebase, Play Store):
#   Store JSON in GITHUB_TOKEN or provider secret; write to disk at runtime.

# Rotate periodically. Scan repos for leaks (git-secrets, TruffleHog).

sections.markdown: ## Common mistakes
**Mistake 1: Building on developer laptops.** No reproducibility; 'works on my machine' bugs; auditors can't verify releases.
**Mistake 2: Signing keys checked into git.** Anyone can sign fraudulent versions of your app + push to store.
**Mistake 3: Slow CI (> 20 min).** Devs stop waiting → skip tests locally → red-main storm.
**Mistake 4: Flaky tests ignored.** Devs re-run until green → tests that don't actually pass.
**Mistake 5: No symbol upload.** Crashlytics reports arrive obfuscated + unreadable.
**Mistake 6: No caching.** Every build re-downloads pub / gradle / cocoapods — 5× the time.
**Mistake 7: Same pipeline for PR + main.** PR builds shouldn't distribute to prod; main builds shouldn't gate on human review.
**Mistake 8: No branch protection.** Merges bypassing CI.
## Best practices
**1. All builds in CI** — never on laptops.
**2. Secrets in provider secret store;** rotate + audit.
**3. Cache pub / gradle / pods** for < 10 min CI.
**4. Symbol upload every release build.**
**5. Separate pipelines per env** (dev / staging / prod).
**6. Coverage threshold** enforced.
**7. Manual approval for prod deploy.**
**8. Reproducible builds** — pinned versions + lockfiles.
## Practice programs
**Practice 1 (Easy)** — GitHub Actions running format + analyze + test on every PR.
**Practice 2 (Medium)** — Add build for Android AAB with obfuscation + symbol upload.
**Practice 3 (Medium)** — Cache pub/gradle/pods; measure CI time delta.
**Practice 4 (Hard)** — Nightly distribution to Firebase App Distribution qa group.
**Practice 5 (Hard)** — Signed iOS build via Fastlane match on CI.
**Practice 6 (Expert)** — Multi-flavor + multi-env pipeline with manual prod approval gate.
## Interview Q&A

**Q1: CI vs Continuous Delivery vs Continuous Deployment?**

**A:** **CI** = build + test every commit + PR, block bad code from merging to main. Answer: 'is this code correct?' **Continuous Delivery** = every green commit produces a DEPLOYABLE artifact; deploy is a manual button. Answer: 'is this code ready to ship?' **Continuous Deployment** = every green commit is automatically shipped to production, no human in the loop. Answer: 'ship it now.' **Mobile reality:** true Continuous Deployment is impossible for store-gated apps (Play + App Store review); most mobile teams do Continuous Delivery + release-cadence deploys. **Backend / web:** true CD is achievable + common at Google/Meta/Netflix. **Interviewer signal:** knowing the D's are DIFFERENT + why mobile is stuck at Delivery.

**Q2: How would you keep a Flutter CI pipeline fast?**

**A:** **Targets:** < 10 min from commit to green. **Techniques:** (1) **Cache dependencies** — pub, gradle, cocoapods; ~5-8 min savings. (2) **Parallelize jobs** — Android build || iOS build; unit tests || integration tests. (3) **Skip unaffected tests** — path-based CI filters or Melos filtering. (4) **Fast runners** — macOS M2 in cloud is 2-3× faster than default; extra cost worth it. (5) **Short critical path** — format + analyze + test = block; build + integration test = post-merge async. (6) **Fail fast** — order steps cheapest → most expensive. (7) **`flutter test --concurrency N`** — parallel test execution. (8) **Pre-built base images** — Docker image with Flutter SDK pre-installed for Linux CI. (9) **Skip iOS on non-iOS-touching PRs** (path filter). (10) **Test sharding** for large suites. **CI time is dev experience** — every 5-min saving compounds across hundreds of PRs/week.

**Q3: How do you handle signing keys + certificates securely?**

**A:** **Android:** (1) Generate `.jks` keystore ONCE, backed up in KMS + team password manager. (2) Base64-encode + store in CI secret. (3) In pipeline, decode to disk + reference from Gradle signing config. (4) NEVER commit `.jks` to git. (5) Rotate every 2-3 years. **iOS:** (1) **Fastlane `match`** — stores certs + provisioning profiles in an encrypted git repo (passphrase in CI secret); syncs to CI + local machines. (2) **App Store Connect API key** for Xcode Cloud + auto-signing. (3) NEVER commit `.p12` or `.mobileprovision`. **General:** (1) Least privilege — CI service accounts have only the roles they need. (2) Rotate on team-member departure. (3) Audit access logs. (4) Store Firebase service-account JSONs as secrets, write to disk at runtime. (5) Signing key compromise → immediate rotation + Play Console + Apple Developer notice. **Interview senior signal:** knowing match + rotation policy.

**Q4: How do you separate dev / staging / prod pipelines?**

**A:** **(1) Flavors** — Flutter build flavors (`dev`, `staging`, `prod`); each with distinct Firebase project + bundle id + app name. **(2) `--dart-define ENV=dev`** — build-time constants inject env-specific config. **(3) `firebase_options_<env>.dart`** — separate files. **(4) Pipelines per branch** — `main` builds dev + distributes to internal; `release/*` builds staging + distributes to beta; tags build prod + submit to store. **(5) Environment secrets** — dev vs prod secrets in separate GitHub Environments (with approval gates). **(6) Distinct CI runners** — staging + prod may run on protected runners with restricted access. **(7) Distinct signing keys per env** — prod key never touches dev pipeline. **(8) Manual approval for prod** — Environment protection rules + required reviewers. **This is the standard mid-large team pattern; senior interviewers respect it.**

**Q5: What are common CI security concerns?**

**A:** **(1) Secret exposure via logs** — `echo $SECRET` prints it. Use `add-mask` or provider-provided secret redaction. **(2) Malicious PR from a fork** — attacker submits PR that exfiltrates secrets via CI. Use `pull_request_target` cautiously; require review before running privileged jobs. **(3) Third-party actions** — a compromised `uses: some-org/action@v1` runs with your secrets. Pin to a commit SHA, not a tag. **(4) Supply-chain attacks** — dependency compromised. Use `pubspec.lock` + Dependabot + npm audit / dart pub audit. **(5) Insecure runners** — self-hosted runners can be persistent; isolate + rotate. **(6) Excessive permissions** — GITHUB_TOKEN grants write by default; set to read-only unless needed. **(7) Cache poisoning** — a compromised cache serves malicious deps. Namespace + scope caches. **(8) Signing key theft** — the ultimate compromise. Hardware security modules for prod signing where possible. **Interviewer bonus:** knowing the OWASP CI/CD Top 10.

**Q6: How would you design a release-quality gate?**

**A:** Before promoting `release/1.2.0` to prod: **(1) All CI green** — build + tests + lint + security scan. **(2) Coverage threshold met** (e.g., 75%+). **(3) Distributed to beta** for at least 3 days with < 0.5% crash-free-users regression on the beta cohort. **(4) Firebase Crashlytics velocity** — no new signature spikes. **(5) Firebase Performance** — cold-start p95 not regressing > 15 % vs prior release. **(6) Analytics conversion funnel** — no drops. **(7) Manual QA sign-off** — checklist executed. **(8) Regulatory checks (pharma / medical)** — appropriate audits passed. **(9) Signed off by product + eng lead.** **(10) Release notes drafted** + reviewed. **(11) Rollback plan documented** — Remote Config kill switch prepared. **Only then** does the pipeline promote to prod. **Automate what you can (metrics), require humans for what you can't (QA sign-off).** Interviewer signal: comprehensive multi-signal gate.

## Real-world usage

- **Every professional Flutter team** — GitHub Actions / Codemagic / Bitrise / CircleCI.
- **Nightly + weekly + release cadence** distribution.
- **Multi-flavor** dev / staging / prod.
- **Quality gates** — coverage + crash-free + perf metrics.
- **NOT ideal for** — solo hobby projects (overhead > benefit until team > 2).

## Advanced notes

- **`workflow_dispatch`** — manually-triggered workflows.
- **`concurrency`** — cancel in-progress runs on new push.
- **`environments`** — GitHub environments with protection rules + required reviewers.
- **`re-usable workflows`** — DRY across repos.
- **`composite actions`** — encapsulate steps.
- **Matrix builds** — Android + iOS + Web in one config.
- **Self-hosted runners** — for macOS at scale, avoid GitHub's per-min charges.
- **Cache best practices** — key by lockfile hash.
- **`actions/upload-artifact` + `download-artifact`** — share artifacts between jobs.
- **Test reporters** — JUnit XML publish for PR annotations.
- **Code coverage** — Codecov / Coveralls / built-in.
- **Security scans** — CodeQL, Snyk, dart pub audit.
- **Renovate / Dependabot** — auto-PRs for dependency updates.
- **Merge queue** — batches PR merges for high-volume repos.
- **Xcode Cloud** — Apple's CI for iOS; integrates with App Store Connect.
- **Codemagic + Bitrise** — Flutter-first CI providers.

Continuous Delivery is the norm; store review breaks Continuous Deployment.
Base64 in CI secret (Android); Fastlane match encrypted git repo (iOS). NEVER in code.
pub / gradle / cocoapods — cuts CI 5-8 min.
